title: Legally enforceable contracts in ADA, in compliance with Argentine laws

ms.promise: This milestone involves the presentation of four comprehensive documents detailing four distinct legal business models applicable in Argentina. Each model will incorporate ADA (Cardano's cryptocurrency) as a payment method. Following thorough research, development, and drafting of four bespoke contracts, the documents will be presented in both English and Spanish.

Once the documents are presented, a separate document will be prepared to outline the legal and technical process, the applicable legal framework, and the credentials of the licensed specialists involved in the review, including their profiles. These documents will be presented in both English and Spanish.

ms.report:
On October 8, 2024, a loan agreement was signed in the district of La Plata before the notary of Registry No. 139 of the Partido de La Plata between Lucas Macchiavelli and Mauro Andreoli. The agreement was formalized through Notarial Deed No. 99. This event garnered significant national and international media attention. The original copies were presented as a gift to Charles Hoskinson during one of his visits to Argentina in the lead-up to the Cardano Constitutional Convention.

Legal framework utilized to achieve this accomplishment.

1. Article 1525 - Concept of a Mutuum Contract (Civil and Commercial Code)

Article 1525 establishes the definition of a mutuum contract, which is a type of loan agreement where the lender (mutuante) agrees to transfer the ownership of a specific quantity of fungible goods to the borrower (mutuario), and the borrower, in turn, commits to returning an equivalent quantity of goods of the same quality and kind. This article is foundational to the agreement, as it provides the legal basis for the loan of ADA in the contract.

Legal Impact: By referencing this article, the contract legally qualifies as a mutuum agreement under Argentine law, with all the rights and obligations that this entails. It legitimizes the transaction structure and provides a clear framework for the restitution of ADA.

2. Article 1526 - Lender's Obligation to Deliver (Civil and Commercial Code)

Article 1526 specifies that the lender is not obligated to deliver the promised amount if, after entering into the contract, there is a change in the borrower’s situation that makes restitution uncertain. This article protects the lender’s position by allowing for the suspension or cancellation of the agreement under certain conditions.
